plan.title: Entropy: Why Hot Coffee Never Heats Itself Back Up
plan.description: Entropy measures how spread out energy is in a system, and the second law says it never decreases in an isolated system. This is why some processes are irreversible.

beats.narration: Why does hot coffee never heat itself back up? The answer is entropy, and it explains why time only runs one way.
Entropy measures how spread out energy is. Low entropy means energy is concentrated in one spot. High entropy means it is dispersed evenly.
The second law of thermodynamics says an isolated system never loses entropy. Energy spreads out until it reaches equilibrium, where entropy is highest.

props.definition: The entropy of an isolated system left alone cannot decrease with time.

beats.narration: That makes some processes irreversible. Coffee cools, but never reheats itself. So whenever energy spreads out, you are watching entropy rise.

props.text: Energy spreads out. It never gathers itself back.
